thesis: A Goblin swarm that is really a spell-count machine: bodies make the mana and set the copy count, cheap spells pointed at Zada turn each body into a card, and one payoff turn cashes the whole board into damage.

stages.label: THE RED FLOOR, AND THE BURST THAT ISN'T LAND
stages.what_it_does: Fifteen land entries and thirty-six copies, of which mana_analysis counts 33 as red sources: Fountainport, Reliquary Tower and War Room tap for {C} only. (It also credits Kher Keep red on a land whose printed mana ability reads '{T}: Add {C}', so 33 is the artifact's figure and an upper bound on it.) Add Sol Ring, Ruby Medallion and Throne of Eldraine. That part only has to hit drops. The part that decides games is the declared ritual group of four, which scales off the board rather than off lands: Battle Hymn adds {R} per creature, Brightstone Ritual {R} per Goblin, Seething Song is flat, Mana Geyser reads the opponents' tapped lands. Once bodies exist, mana is downstream of the body count. (The taxonomy reads ramp:ritual at 6, adding Ancestors' Aid and Glimpse the Impossible; this model files the second of those in fuel.) The brief's goldfish figure for turn five is 4.589 mean available mana — nowhere near a storm turn, which is the point: the big turn is bought with a ritual cast into an existing board, not with land drops. Goblin Warchief sits here as a cost reducer rather than with the Goblins: stack 004 locked Krenko at {1}{R}{R} because of it, and the haste it grants is what let Krenko tap the turn he landed. Ancestors' Aid is filed here because through the hub its Treasure clause is a Treasure per creature — a ritual with a pump stapled on. The utility lands are mostly NOT here for their mana: Reliquary Tower's 'no maximum hand size' is why a deck that draws five cards off one {R} (stack 001) plays a colourless land, War Room's '{3}, {T}, pay life: draw a card' is repeatable advantage that deck-audit lists under card-advantage's uncounted, and Fountainport turns a spent token into a card.

evidence.note: Goblin Warchief's static reduction locks Krenko's total cost at {1}{R}{R} and grants the haste that allows the same-turn tap
THE RED FLOOR is exactly the fifteen land entries and nothing else; the stage is larger
the rituals and Ancestors' Aid live in MANA FOR ONE TURN, the rocks and Warchief in THE STAYING POWER, Seething Song in CRITICAL MASS

stages.label: A SECOND AND THIRD BODY BY TURN THREE
stages.what_it_does: Every multiplier in this deck multiplies by the number of creatures already on the battlefield. Zada with an empty board copies nothing. Brightstone Ritual adds one {R}. Impact Tremors fires once. So the first thing that has to happen is not the hub and not a ritual — it is bodies, cheaply, early. Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command are two 1/1s for two mana; Mogg War Marshal is two over its life and replaces itself when it dies; Searslicer Goblin is one more at every end step you attacked. The brief prices the declared group at 5 cards, 31.2% in an opener and 38.6% by turn three, assembling 60% of games at mean turn 3.184 — the earliest of the three declared targets by 1.730 turns against the next-earliest, the storm payoff plus ritual at mean turn 4.914, and the reason this deck can afford a five-mana payoff. The declared group's fifth card is Skirk Prospector, which creates no tokens; it is held in conversion here, where it eats them, and that difference is filed as a proposed goldfish edit so the price and the stage can agree.

evidence.note: Dragon Fodder is one of the three prior casts that set Empty the Warrens' storm count at 3

all four sit inside THE TOKEN FACTORY. Exactly two stages in this model live at one address — this one, and protection, whose two cards are both in THE STAYING POWER. Ignition is the only one of the two that does work rather than carry insurance
the declared component's shared roles are threat:tokens and threat:body — a property of the cards, not evidence that they interact

stages.label: CHEAP SPELLS THAT REPLACE THEMSELVES
stages.what_it_does: Storm counts CASTS, and stack 002 established the hard half of that: copies are put on the stack without being cast, so a storm count of 3 becomes 8 tokens but the next spell still only sees 4. Nothing here can be replaced by a copy — every point of count has to be paid for one card at a time, which is why this is the largest non-mana stage. Crimson Wisps, Expedite and Renegade Tactics cost {R} and cantrip on their own; pointed at the hub they draw one card per body (stack 001: five cards off a single {R} with four Goblins out). Witch's Mark, Faithless Looting, Glimpse the Impossible and Daring Discovery are the deck's paper card advantage, and not one of them refills a hand: Faithless Looting is draw two then discard two, net zero and a filter; Witch's Mark is net +1 and gated on already holding a card to pitch, which is the resource a storm turn has just spent; Glimpse the Impossible exiles three cards playable only this turn; Daring Discovery is Discover 4, which is one card. deck-audit reads card-advantage at 8 copies against a floor of 10, verdict under. The rule above therefore has no exception. Goblin Matron and Moggcatcher find the missing piece; Conspicuous Snoop casts Goblins off the top of the library. Past in Flames gives flashback to every instant and sorcery in the graveyard, which after a storm turn is where the whole hand went: that is the rebuild plan, and it is one card. Goblin Dark-Dwellers recasts exactly one spell, and only at mana value 3 or less — a far smaller second option, not redundancy for it. Grenzo turns combat damage into impulse cards. Witch's Mark is also a legal Zada target and is absent from the declared cantrip component; that is filed as a proposed goldfish edit.

evidence.note: Crimson Wisps targeting only Zada with four Goblins out: four copies plus the original, five cards drawn
the copies of Empty the Warrens are not cast, so a later Grapeshot sees storm count 4 and not 7
ten of the thirteen are in CRITICAL MASS
Faithless Looting and Witch's Mark cluster on their draw text in THE STAYING POWER; Glimpse the Impossible on its Eldrazi Spawn mana in MANA FOR ONE TURN

stages.label: THE BODY PILE
stages.what_it_does: Goblins are the resource this deck converts, and they are spent four different ways: counted (Zada's copy count, Brightstone Ritual, Battle Hymn, Impact Tremors), sacrificed for mana or damage, clamped for cards, and pumped for lethal. So the pile is a stage in its own right rather than a threat count. Krenko, Mob Boss is the largest single producer — stack 004 measured one activation at five tokens, because Krenko counts himself — four Goblins were out when he was cast and five when the ability resolved — leaving ten Goblins on the table. Howlsquad Heavy and Goblin Chieftain hand the pile haste, which matters because most of these bodies are made on the turn they are meant to be spent. Goblin Chieftain, Rundvelt Hordemaster and Goblin Trashmaster are lords: they raise what every 1/1 is worth in combat and, in Hordemaster's case, turn Goblin deaths back into cards. Goblin Lackey puts a Goblin permanent onto the battlefield off first-strike-free combat damage; Impulsive Pilferer is a body that becomes a Treasure when it dies; Redcap Gutter-Dweller brings two Rats and eats a creature every upkeep. Nothing here is a win condition on its own, and that is the correct reading of it.

evidence.note: Krenko cast under Warchief, tapping the same turn for five tokens; the board goes to ten Goblins
four in CRITICAL MASS, Krenko in THE TOKEN FACTORY, Howlsquad Heavy and Impulsive Pilferer in MANA FOR ONE TURN, Goblin Trashmaster in BODIES INTO DAMAGE

stages.label: THE HUBS — ONE RESOURCE IN, A DIFFERENT ONE OUT
stages.what_it_does: Seven cards that take one resource and hand back another, cheaply and repeatably. Zada is the multiplier: an instant or sorcery targeting only her is copied once per other creature, so the board size is the exchange rate (stack 001: four copies plus the original off one {R}). Frontline Heroism is redundancy for the EFFECT and not for the multiplier — read the text, it makes one Soldier and copies the spell once, at that token, however wide you are. Storm-Kiln Artist turns every cast and every copy into a Treasure, which is what makes the buyback loop mana-positive in stack 005. Skirk Prospector eats a Goblin for {R} — stack 004 measured at most ten, one shot, and it empties the board doing it. Skullclamp turns a 1/1 into two cards, which is why a sweeper is a draw step here. Goblin Bombardment is the free outlet, converting any body into a point of damage at instant speed. Idol of Oblivion draws one card per TURN, gated on having created a token — the one rate in this paragraph that is not per unit. Zada is this stage's single point of failure and the brief agrees from the other side: she is the only load-bearing card in the deck, the one card named by two passing stacks. Being the commander makes an answer a tax rather than a loss, but nothing else in the 99 multiplies, so the tax is charged every time the engine restarts. This is the stage the map cannot see: its seven cards have four different city addresses, because a card's text names what it pays and never what it eats.

evidence.note: the copy count is the board count: four Goblin tokens, four copies
Prospector converts up to ten Goblins into one-shot red mana; the combo graph's infinite is refuted here because Zada, not Krenko, is the commander
magecraft mints a Treasure per cast AND per copy: four on cast #1, five on cast #2, nine on board
Zada and Goblin Bombardment in BODIES INTO DAMAGE, Storm-Kiln and Prospector in MANA FOR ONE TURN, Skullclamp in THE STAYING POWER, Frontline Heroism and Idol of Oblivion in THE TOKEN FACTORY

stages.label: WHERE IT LANDS
stages.what_it_does: Impact Tremors and General Kreat, the Boltbringer are the two cards in the 99 that turn a creature entering into damage to EACH opponent, and the deck's best-verified kill runs straight through them: stack 002 resolves eight tokens into eight damage to each of two opponents. Neither is a single point of failure on its own — that is why this stage declares none — but two cards is thinner than anything the declaration prices — the thinnest declared component is four cards at 25.8% in an opener — and no goldfish target measures this class at all. Boggart Shenanigans and Pashalik Mons price Goblin deaths instead, one point per death at a chosen target, which is the reach that survives a sweeper. Siege-Gang Commander, Siege-Gang Lieutenant and Broadside Bombardiers buy damage with a body at a cost, and all three can point it at a player. Gempalm Incinerator and Goblin Negotiation spend no body and are not that class: Incinerator is cycled from hand for X equal to the Goblin count, so bodies are the meter rather than the fuel, and Negotiation MAKES tokens out of excess damage. Both can only hit a creature, so neither is reach across a table. Grapeshot is filed here rather than in wincon deliberately: stack 002 measured it at storm count 4, which is five instances of one damage — real reach and real creature removal, and not a kill across three seats at forty life. Chaos Warp, Vandalblast and Blasphemous Act are the interaction budget, and Blasphemous Act is a reset that this deck survives better than most.

evidence.note: eight Impact Tremors triggers, eight damage to each opponent; the following Grapeshot sees storm count 4
ten of the thirteen are BODIES INTO DAMAGE; Chaos Warp and Vandalblast sit in CRITICAL MASS and Blasphemous Act in THE STAYING POWER

stages.label: ONE PAIR OF BOOTS
stages.what_it_does: The brief's audit axis reads 2 copies against a 5-7 target, and reading the two cards makes it thinner than that. Swiftfoot Boots grants hexproof and haste to a creature and equips for {1}. Roaming Throne's ward {2} protects Roaming Throne — it is insurance for itself, not for the hub. So exactly one card in the 99 can make Zada untargetable, and the deck's real answer to a removal spell is the commander tax plus the fact that half the engine never needed her: the rituals, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot and the Haze of Rage / Storm-Kiln loop all function with Zada in the command zone. That is a genuine structural strength and it is also why the insurance is affordable at one card. Roaming Throne is placed here on its ward. If its trigger-doubling clause, with Goblin chosen, applies to Zada's copy trigger, it is a conversion piece worth twice what it looks like, and that question is open and unresolved.

evidence.note: the taxonomy gives both cards protection:self — a property of each card, and precisely the reason neither covers a third permanent
both sit in THE STAYING POWER, which is eleven cards wide and mostly not protection

stages.label: THE ONE TURN, THREE WAYS
stages.what_it_does: Three endings, and all three have a checker-passed board behind them. Fists of Flame through the hub is the burst: stack 003 resolves copies one at a time, each drawing first, so the +1/+0-per-card locks in at +3/+4/+5/+6 on the tokens and +7 on Zada — 32 power with trample, at least 30 of it reaching an opponent at 30 life past a lone 2/2. Empty the Warrens is the wide ending: stack 002 turns storm count 3 into eight tokens. Haze of Rage with Storm-Kiln Artist is the arbitrary one: stack 005 verifies two buyback casts at +9/+0 across the team and nine Treasures, with each further iteration costing four and yielding k+3 — mana-positive and strictly improving. Wild Ride, Goblin Bushwhacker, Great Train Heist and Quest for the Goblin Lord are the smaller pumps that convert an existing swarm; Spreading Insurrection steals a creature per storm copy. Note that the declared 'storm payoff' component is split by this model: three of its four cards end games and Grapeshot is reach, which is a disagreement with the declaration rather than with the map.

evidence.note: 32 total power with trample; the buffs do not grow retroactively, so the ORDER of resolution sets the size
storm count 3 produces eight tokens across four resolutions
the loop is mana-positive from cast #2 and strictly improves; the Commander Spellbook line is confirmed for this pair

Dragon Fodder is one of the three casts before Empty the Warrens in the verified board, and storm count is all it pays there: stack 002's board is Impact Tremors and four Mountains with zero Goblin tokens on it, so the stack shows the token maker paying once, not twice

map_disagreements.component: Zada online with a cantrip drawn (declared)
map_disagreements.why: the group's defining property is a LEGALITY — cheap enough to cast and worded so it can target only one creature you control — and no card says that anywhere in its text. The map reads each card's other half instead: Ancestors' Aid on its Treasure clause, Fists of Flame on its draw-and-pump. Four of the six land together only because they are all one-mana red spells

Skirk Prospector is filed under mana because its text says 'Add {R}', which is exactly the reason it does not belong in a token-maker group — it creates no tokens, it eats them. Here the map is right and the declaration is wrong, which is the inverse of the usual case

map_disagreements.component: Storm payoff plus ritual drawn — the payoff half (declared)
map_disagreements.why: the shared property is one keyword, storm, and clustering reads what each spell DOES: Grapeshot with the burn, Empty the Warrens with the token makers, Haze of Rage and Spreading Insurrection with the cheap red spells. A keyword that modifies how many times a spell happens is invisible to a model of what the spell does

an exchange engine is defined by what it eats and what it pays, and card text names only the payment. Zada is filed with the damage cards, Skullclamp with the cheap-spells-and-hand city, Storm-Kiln Artist and Skirk Prospector with the mana. The engine proper has four addresses and no territory, which is the single most useful thing the map cannot tell you about this deck

map_disagreements.component: wincon — the one turn (this model's stage)
map_disagreements.why: the deck has three different endings — a trample burst, a token flood into each-opponent damage, and an unbounded pump loop — and they have nothing in common in card text. The brief's own scatter table says it plainly: 0 of 4 declared components sit in a single city

open_questions.question: Can a stack scenario verify the Empty the Warrens -> Impact Tremors arrow under the citation contract? Stack 002 resolves it (eight tokens, eight damage to each opponent) but names Impact Tremors only on the battlefield, and `line_cards` skips the board when the stack, hand and graveyard already name two or more cards — so the deck's headline kill has no citable link between the token flood and the damage.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Impact Tremors is one of only two cards in the 99 that convert a creature entering into damage to each opponent, and the arrow that says so currently has to render dashed. Three columnists are forbidden to assert an unverified line, so this gap reaches the prose.

open_questions.question: With Goblin chosen, does Roaming Throne's 'triggers an additional time' clause apply to Zada's copy trigger — and if it does, how many copies result: 2N, or N doubled with each set choosing targets separately?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether Roaming Throne belongs in protection (ward on itself, which is where this model put it) or in conversion as a second multiplier. It is a four-mana card either way, but the two readings differ by a factor of two on every hub turn.

open_questions.question: Does Frontline Heroism's copy clause behave as the strategic frame describes it — a second copy hub? Read literally it creates one Soldier and copies the spell once, at that token, regardless of board width, which is one extra copy rather than one per creature.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only in-deck redundancy for the copy effect. If it makes one copy and not N, the deck's answer to a removed Zada is far weaker than the declaration's commander-gated target implies, and the thinnest component in the deck is the hub itself.

open_questions.question: What rate does the deck assemble the stack-002 kill — an each-opponent ETB damage payoff (Impact Tremors or General Kreat) together with a token maker — by turn six? No declared target measures this pair at all.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's best-verified path to damage across three seats, and the simulator has never been pointed at it. The three declared targets measure the hub's ammunition, an early body and a payoff-plus-ritual; none of them measures the thing stack 002 proves.

open_questions.question: Does the strategy doc's commander-insurance target (deck-audit reads 2 copies against 5-7) apply to a commander whose engine is OPTIONAL? Half of this deck — rituals, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot, the Haze of Rage loop — functions with Zada in the command zone.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the target assumes a must-resolve commander, the axis is measuring this deck against the wrong standard and a pilot will buy protection slots the deck does not need. If it does not, one pair of Boots is a real hole.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either rename the label to 'Early Goblin body drawn', or replace Skirk Prospector with a card that actually makes tokens. Prospector creates none — it is a one-mana Goblin body and a sacrifice outlet.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: As declared, the group's size-5 pricing (31.2% in an opener, 38.6% by turn three) measures 'an early Goblin body', which is a looser claim than the label makes. The deck's own map agrees: Prospector clusters in MANA FOR ONE TURN, away from the other four.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Zada online with a cantrip drawn
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Witch's Mark to the any_of group, taking it from 6 cards to 7.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Witch's Mark targets 'up to one target creature you control', so it can be cast targeting only Zada, and it draws two. The strategic frame already names it among the cantrips; the goldfish group omits it. Price the change against this component's own odds and not the nearest citable anchor: engine-facts puts the declared 6-card group at 36.4% of openers, and the cited redundancy anchor puts 7 copies at 41.1%. The 5-copy figure of 31% is not this edit's baseline.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: a new target: 'Each-opponent ETB damage payoff plus a token maker'
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Declare a target with two any_of groups: [Impact Tremors, General Kreat, the Boltbringer] and the early-token-maker group, so the simulator measures the pair stack 002 proves.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: This is the primary-win-line-with-no-target defect the fleet has hit twice before. The deck's best-verified kill runs through a two-card class, thinner than any declared component (the thinnest priced group is 4 cards at 25.8%), and nothing measures it.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: a new target: 'The copy hub without the commander'
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Declare a target whose only any_of group is [Frontline Heroism], and leave the existing 'Zada online' target commander-gated as it is.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The existing hub target sets commander: true, so the simulator assumes the multiplier and measures only its ammunition. The deck's real exposure is the turn after Zada is answered, and its in-deck redundancy for that effect is one card — a size-1 group is exactly the redundancy claim being made. It also gives deck-audit something to price: this model declares Zada as conversion's single point of failure, while audit_engine.single_points_of_failure is empty because no declared target names her.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Storm-Kiln Artist to the ritual any_of group, or declare the loop as its own target [Haze of Rage] + [Storm-Kiln Artist].
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Stack 005 is the deck's only verified arbitrarily-large line and Storm-Kiln Artist appears in no component at all. It is also a Treasure engine that pays for the storm turn, which is the same job as the four cards already in that group.

findings.claim: Fifteen land entries, thirty-six copies, all of them red
findings.note: mana_analysis.json reads sources.lands.R = 33 against lands.total = 36. Three land copies produce no red at all and the model NAMES all three two sentences later in its own utility-land list: Fountainport, Reliquary Tower and War Room each read '{T}: Add {C}' and each carries produces: [] in mana_analysis's lands.list. Entries and copies (15 / 36) are both exact; only 'all of them red' is wrong. Worse than a rounding error, because the sentence is the stage's opening premise and a mono-red deck's red-source count is the one figure a reader will not re-check. Note in passing that a fourth, Kher Keep, also taps for {C} by its oracle text while mana_analysis credits it R — so the defensible number is 32-33, never 36. Mechanically checkable: a stage's colour claim can be diffed against mana_analysis.sources.lands.

findings.claim: all four sit inside THE TOKEN FACTORY, the only stage in this model that lives at one address
findings.note: This is in stages[1].evidence[1].note and it is contradicted by stages[6].evidence[1].note in the same file: protection's two cards BOTH sit in THE STAYING POWER. Joining engine.json's stages to deck_map.json's level-0 regions gives distinct-city counts of mana 4, ignition 1, fuel 3, fodder 4, conversion 4, output 3, protection 1, wincon 4. Two stages live at one address, not one. Ignition is still the only MULTI-card functional stage that does, if that is the claim intended — but as written the model asserts something its own protection evidence denies. Mechanically checkable: count distinct level-0 regions per stage and compare against any 'only stage' phrasing.

findings.claim: the earliest of the three declared targets by two full turns
findings.note: goldfish_metrics.json mean_turn: 'Early token maker drawn' 3.184, 'Storm payoff plus ritual drawn' 4.914, 'Zada online with a cantrip drawn' 5.266. Earliest by 1.730 turns against the next-earliest. 'By two full turns' is only reachable against the LATEST target (2.082), which is not what 'the earliest of the three ... by' means. The 0.27-turn overstatement is small; the sentence it props up is not — it is the stage's argument for why a five-mana payoff is affordable. 1.7 turns still carries that argument, so this costs the model nothing to fix.

findings.claim: conversion declares no single point of failure
findings.note: The model argues the opposite in three other places. open_questions[2] concludes 'the thinnest component in the deck is the hub itself'; proposed_goldfish_edits[3] asks for a size-1 group precisely so deck-audit can 'price a single point of failure it currently reports as zero'; and stages[4].what_it_does establishes that Frontline Heroism is 'redundancy for the EFFECT and not for the multiplier'. engine-facts agrees from the other side: verified.load_bearing_cards is exactly ['Zada, Hedron Grinder'], the only card in two passing stacks. Either Zada is conversion's single_point_of_failure or the proposed edit's justification is wrong; the model cannot hold both. The available rebuttal is real and should be written down if taken: a commander is recastable from the command zone, so she is a tax rather than a loss — but then edit[3] must stop calling her a single point of failure. Note the asymmetry this creates today: protection declares a SPOF for a stage the model calls optional, while conversion declares none for the card the whole engine turns on.

findings.claim: Witch's Mark, Faithless Looting, Glimpse the Impossible and Daring Discovery refill the hand outright
findings.note: Against cards.json oracle text, none of the four refills a hand outright. Faithless Looting is 'Draw two cards, then discard two cards' — net ZERO, a filter, and the single worst member of a class defined by refilling. Witch's Mark is 'You may discard a card. If you do, draw two cards' — net +1 and GATED on already holding a card, which is exactly the resource a storm turn has spent. Glimpse the Impossible exiles three playable only this turn, converting the remainder to 0/1 Spawn — impulse with a clock, not hand. Daring Discovery is Discover 4: one card. The claim matters because the same paragraph's argument is that 'every point of count has to be paid for one card at a time', and this sentence is the stated exception to it. deck-audit independently reads card-advantage at 8 copies against a floor of 10, verdict 'under'.

findings.claim: Siege-Gang Commander, Siege-Gang Lieutenant, Broadside Bombardiers, Gempalm Incinerator and Goblin Negotiation buy damage with a body at a cost
findings.note: Three of the five do. Siege-Gang Commander ('{1}{R}, Sacrifice a Goblin: 2 damage to any target'), Siege-Gang Lieutenant ('{2}, Sacrifice a Goblin: 1 damage to any target') and Broadside Bombardiers ('Sacrifice another creature or artifact') all spend a body. Gempalm Incinerator spends NO body — it is cycled from hand and deals X to a creature where X is the Goblin count, which is the opposite trade (bodies are the meter, not the fuel). Goblin Negotiation spends no body either and CREATES them: 'deals X damage to target creature. Create a number of 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens equal to the amount of excess damage'. Both non-members also share a restriction the sentence hides: they can only hit a creature, never a player, so neither is reach across a table. Two of five wrong, both in the same direction, inside the stage whose job is stating how the deck converts bodies into damage.

findings.claim: The brief's cited redundancy anchors put 7 copies at 41.1% of openers against 5 at 31%
findings.note: The quoted anchors are real (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors, verbatim in engine-facts.audit_engine.redundancy_citation) but they are the wrong pair. The edit itself says the group goes 'from 6 cards to 7', and engine-facts prices that same 6-card component at opening_seven 0.364. The gain being bought is 36.4% -> 41.1%, i.e. +4.7 points, not 31% -> 41.1%, i.e. +10.1. Quoting the 5-copy anchor doubles the apparent value of an edit that is still worth making — the recomputed 41.1% is right, the baseline is not. Mechanically checkable: an edit that changes a component's size must price the change against that component's own engine-facts odds, not against the nearest citable anchor.

findings.claim: an early token maker pays twice, once in bodies and once in count
findings.note: The carries value ('storm count') is exactly right and stack 002 establishes it: extras.spells_cast_before_this_turn is 3, the graveyard holds exactly three cards, and build_index.line_cards resolves 002 to [Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Dragon Fodder, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot], so Dragon Fodder being one of the three prior casts is corroborated rather than assumed. The 'once in bodies' half is not. Stack 002's board is 'Impact Tremors, Mountain x4' — ZERO Goblin tokens — and the opponents open at 32 and 28 with no Impact Tremors damage yet taken, i.e. the verified board is one in which Dragon Fodder contributed no bodies at all to the kill. The stack shows the token maker paying exactly ONCE, in count. (The scenario is arguably inconsistent with itself on this point; that is the stack's problem, but the model may not borrow the half of it the board denies.)

findings.claim: stack 004 measured one activation off a four-Goblin board at five tokens
findings.note: Stack 004 step 5 is explicit: 'X is determined now, at resolution: you control 5 Goblins (Krenko, Warchief, Prospector, 2 tokens), so X = 5'. The board was four Goblins before Krenko was CAST and five when the ability RESOLVED — Krenko counts himself. As written the sentence teaches the reader X = board count, off by one in the direction that happens to give the right answer here and the wrong one everywhere else. 'Leaving ten Goblins on the table' is exact (step 5). Fix is one clause: five, because Krenko counts himself.

findings.claim: Goblin Dark-Dwellers and Past in Flames recast the graveyard ... that is the deck's rebuild plan, and it is two cards deep
findings.note: Past in Flames gives flashback to EVERY instant and sorcery in the yard. Goblin Dark-Dwellers casts exactly one, and only at mana value 3 or less. Calling them a two-deep class treats an order-of-magnitude difference as redundancy — the same mistake the model correctly refuses to make one stage later about Frontline Heroism, and worth flagging for the same reason: a rebuild plan that reads 'two cards deep' will be quoted as redundancy by the prose.

findings.claim: Idol of Oblivion pays a card for a token made
findings.note: Oracle text is '{T}: Draw a card. Activate only if you created a token this turn.' It is one card per TURN, gated on having made any token — not one card per token, which is what a hub stage's 'one resource in, a different one out' framing implies and what the surrounding sentences (Skullclamp two cards per body, Bombardment one damage per body) set the reader up to expect. It is the only per-unit rate in the paragraph that is not per-unit.

findings.claim: The utility lands (War Room, Fountainport, Reliquary Tower, Spinerock Knoll, Kher Keep) ... none of them is why they are in the deck
findings.note: Backwards for at least two of the five. Reliquary Tower's mana ability is the throwaway — 'You have no maximum hand size' is the reason a deck that draws five cards off one {R} (stack 001) runs it. War Room is '{3}, {T}, Pay life: Draw a card', and deck-audit lists it under card-advantage's possible_uncounted for exactly that. Neither is in the deck for its {C}. Related smaller slip in the same paragraph: 'the four rituals' is stated three sentences before the model itself describes Ancestors' Aid as 'a ritual with a pump stapled on', and deck-audit counts ramp:ritual at 6.

findings.claim: the deck's headline kill and it is NOT verifiable as drawn
findings.note: Checked against the code rather than taken on trust, because this is the one place a model could talk itself out of evidence it holds. build_index.line_cards collects stack + hand + graveyard first and returns as soon as that reaches two names; stack 002's stack/hand/graveyard yield five, so the board is skipped and Impact Tremors never enters the list. engine-facts confirms it independently: verified.by_stack['002'].cards is exactly [Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Dragon Fodder, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot]. validate-engine requires the cited stack to NAME the via cards, so verified_by: null is forced, not chosen. Two things the model deserves credit for: it did not re-point the via at two cards 002 does name in order to buy a green arrow, and open_questions[0] dispatches the right remedy (a scenario naming Impact Tremors on the stack or in hand). The honest dashed line is correct.

findings.claim: the three Krenko lines assume Krenko is the commander and stack 004 refutes them here
findings.note: Checked for quiet re-adoption, since this deck's record contains a refuted famous infinite. engine-facts.candidate_lines carries four lines, three of them Krenko + Skirk Prospector + (Goblin Chieftain | Goblin Warchief | Howlsquad Heavy), all with assumes_commander: true. Nothing in the model re-adopts them. The refutation is stated three times and consistently — stages[4].evidence[1], lines[7].note and this entry — and each states the actual reason (903.9a scopes the command-zone return to a commander; Zada is the commander; Krenko is also already tapped, so the loop cannot even repeat on the battlefield). lines[7] then prices the surviving line correctly at 'at most ten {R}, one shot', matching stack 004 step 6 verbatim.

findings.claim: Frontline Heroism ... makes one Soldier and copies the spell once, at that token, however wide you are
findings.note: Oracle text in cards.json: 'Whenever you cast a spell that targets only a single creature you control, create a 1/1 red Soldier creature token with haste, then copy that spell. The copy targets that token.' One token, one copy, no per-creature clause — the model's reading is right and the strategic frame's 'second copy hub' is not. This is the most consequential rules reading in the file, because it is what makes open_questions[2] and the hub's thinness argument true rather than rhetorical.

findings.claim: Impact Tremors and General Kreat, the Boltbringer are the two cards in the 99 that turn a creature entering into damage to EACH opponent
findings.note: Scanned all 79 entries for 'each opponent'. Four cards contain the phrase; only these two trigger on a creature entering and deal DAMAGE. Witch's Mark's Wicked Role makes each opponent LOSE 1 life, and only when the Role token hits a graveyard; Impulsive Pilferer's is 'for each opponent' inside an encore cost. The class really is two cards wide, no goldfish target measures it (all three declared targets checked), and proposed_goldfish_edits[2] is therefore the highest-value item in the file.

findings.claim: the only card in the 99 that can make the hub untargetable
findings.note: Scanned all 79 entries for hexproof / shroud / protection from / ward / "can't be the target". Exactly two hits: Swiftfoot Boots and Roaming Throne, and Roaming Throne's ward {2} protects only Roaming Throne, as stages[6] says. Worth stating in the note that hexproof does not stop the pilot's OWN targeting, so Boots and Zada's trigger are compatible — the arrow is drawn backward for the right reason. Mechanically checkable across the fleet: an 'only card that protects X' claim can be diffed against a protection-keyword scan of cards.json.

findings.claim: the Haze of Rage <-> Storm-Kiln Artist feedback pair
findings.note: Both directions are established by stack 005, which is what a backward arrow has to earn. Forward (conversion -> wincon, 'Treasures'): steps 7 and 10 give 4 Treasures on cast #1 and 5 on cast #2, nine on board — the model's figure exactly. Backward (wincon -> conversion, 'casts and copies'): step 4 establishes that each COPY is a magecraft trigger under 112.1a, and step 11 closes the loop, 'iteration k ... costs 4 mana, and yields k+3 Treasures'. The model's 'each further iteration costing four and yielding k+3' is verbatim correct. This is a genuine loop, not two arrows drawn between the same two boxes.

findings.claim: the Zada <-> Crimson Wisps feedback pair
findings.note: Stack 001 establishes both halves: one {R} in (step 1) and five cards out across four copies plus the original (steps 4-8, final_state cards_drawn 5). 'Five hasted bodies' is also right, though they are five EXISTING creatures gaining haste rather than five new ones — worth one word if the line is revised, not a defect.

findings.claim: two notes that state what their stack does NOT show
findings.note: Recording these because they are the behaviour this loop exists to produce. lines[3] carries 'storm count, not mana' out of the mana stage and says outright that 002's four mana come from Mountains with both rituals already in the graveyard — 'The mana claim is not what the stack shows.' lines[5] caps stack 003 at 'One seat, an empty opposing board apart from that blocker — the stack proves a kill, not a table kill', which is exactly what 003's scenario supports (one opponent, 30 life, a lone 2/2). Both are the radagast Castle-Garenbrig failure caught before it was written.

findings.claim: five disagreements, and 0 of 4 declared components sit in a single city
findings.note: Every city list was re-derived from deck_map.json's level-0 regions and every one is exact. Declared cantrip group: CRITICAL MASS 4 / MANA FOR ONE TURN 1 (Ancestors' Aid) / THE STAYING POWER 1 (Fists of Flame). Payoff half: CRITICAL MASS 2 / BODIES INTO DAMAGE 1 (Grapeshot) / THE TOKEN FACTORY 1 (Empty the Warrens). conversion: 2/2/2/1 across four cities exactly as stages[4].evidence[3] says. wincon: 5/1/1/1. engine-facts.scatter carries coherent: false on all four components, so '0 of 4' is right. Each entry also names which artifact is wrong about what rather than hedging — map_disagreements[1] is the best of them ('Here the map is right and the declaration is wrong, which is the inverse of the usual case'). Every other city figure in the file was checked too and all hold: THE RED FLOOR is exactly the fifteen land entries and nothing else; ten of thirteen in fuel and ten of thirteen in output; four in fodder's CRITICAL MASS; rocks and Warchief in THE STAYING POWER; Seething Song in CRITICAL MASS.

findings.claim: structural checks: coverage, length, and the declared figures
findings.note: 79 cards placed, each exactly once, all in the 99, none unassigned — verified against cards.json. what_it_does lengths are 913 / 973 / 1110 / 1111 / 1087 / 1217 / 913 / 1058, every one comfortably under MAX_WHAT_IT_DOES = 1800, so nothing here is at the length where a revision starts failing. Figures re-derived and correct: goldfish turn-five mean available mana 4.589; the 5-card token group at 31.2% opener / 38.6% by turn three / 0.600 assembled / mean turn 3.184; the thinnest declared component at 4 cards and 25.8%; deck-audit protection at 2 copies against the 5-7 target; audit_engine.single_points_of_failure empty. The hypergeometrics behind 25.8 / 31.2 / 38.6 / 41.1 were recomputed by hand and all four land on the printed value.

findings.claim: Roaming Throne with Goblin chosen may double Zada's copy trigger
findings.note: Well-founded, and worth confirming because it decides a stage assignment. Zada's type line is 'Legendary Creature — Goblin Ally', so a Throne naming Goblin reaches her; the Throne's clause is 'If a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type triggers, it triggers an additional time', and Zada's copy ability is a triggered ability of another creature. The question is genuinely open — and the second half the model asks (2N, or N doubled with each set choosing targets separately) is the part that actually matters, since 'could target' is evaluated per trigger. Correctly routed to resolve-stack, and correctly NOT used to move Roaming Throne into conversion in the meantime.
